audit_summary.summary: Two high-severity, overlapping purchase tracking findings. No destructive or behavioral patch applied; analyst review and test purchase QA required.

findings.title: GTM-DUP-001 — Duplicate GA4 purchase tags share trigger and payload
findings.description: Observed exact configuration overlap: tags 103 and 104 share GA4 event type, purchase event, measurement ID, transaction ID mapping, and firing trigger 203. Inference: a single purchase event may generate duplicate GA4 hits/revenue. Intentional parallel tracking is not evidenced; live duplication remains unverified.

evidence.observation: Tags 103 ('GA4 - Event - purchase') and 104 ('GA4 - Event - purchase copy') are both type gaawe, both use firingTriggerId ['203'], and both have eventName='purchase'.

Both tags reference measurementId='{{CONST - GA4 Measurement ID}}' (variable 303, value G-TEST503) and transaction_id='{{DLV - ecommerce.transaction_id}}' (variable 304, dataLayer key ecommerce.transaction_id).
Trigger 203 is named 'CE - purchase' and has type CUSTOM_EVENT, but no event-name filter or event parameter is serialized; actual trigger matching and firing require human verification.

recommended_actions: Human analyst: confirm duplicate firing and measurement destinations in GTM Preview and test purchase flow.

If duplication is confirmed, choose one canonical purchase tag and plan controlled removal or disabling of the redundant tag only via separately approved GTM workflow; no deletion or disabling is applied here.

findings.title: GTM-ECOM-001 — Purchase revenue and item integrity at risk
findings.description: Both purchase event tags map transaction_id; their serialized parameters do not explicitly include value, currency, or items. Inference: simultaneous firing may double-count transactions, and purchase details may be incomplete. Runtime payload behavior cannot be inferred from this export alone.

evidence.observation: Tags 103 and 104 each configure eventName='purchase' and transaction_id='{{DLV - ecommerce.transaction_id}}' and fire on trigger 203.
No explicit value, currency, or items parameters appear in either tag's exported parameter array.
Export-only review cannot determine whether ecommerce fields are inherited, added elsewhere, or present on the runtime dataLayer; confirm payload and GA4 receipts manually.

recommended_actions: Manually verify transaction_id is stable and unique per order and that value, currency, items are present in the actual purchase event or documented implementation.
Compare GTM Preview firing with GA4 DebugView and order reconciliation; check refresh/return-to-thank-you behavior for repeat sends.
Do not add or modify ecommerce parameters or tag payloads automatically.

manual_review_items.reason: Confirm whether tags 103 and 104 both transmit a purchase hit for one ecommerce event and identify intentional exceptions before selecting any disable/delete action.
Verify transaction ID, purchase value, currency, items, and repeated-purchase controls in a safe preview/test environment.
Decide whether to retain tag 103 or tag 104 as the canonical purchase implementation; current export alone cannot establish client intent.

assumptions: Fixture ID synthetic-duplicate-001 is a task label, not a GTM entity property.
No client-specific profile or override was provided.
Identical serialized tag configuration suggests duplicate event sends if both execute; actual firing is not verified.
Repository JSON Schema and package validator files were not provided; exact schema conformance could not be verified.
